mutant.description: The AC2 untouched-canonical control is a fingerprint over size + full-ISO mtime. A control that cannot detect a change is indistinguishable from one whose subject did not change, so the method was PLANTED against: a byte-identical COPY of the canonical DB (canon_copy_db, 82,661,376 B) was mutated with `touch` -- an mtime-only change that preserves size AND content, i.e. the SMALLEST mutation the method must still catch -- and the same fingerprint was recomputed. The real canonical was never touched; it was read by the same method in the same instant as a simultaneous negative control.
mutant.expected: the copy's fingerprint CHANGES after the touch (proving the method detects even a content-preserving mutation), while the real canonical's fingerprint stays 711b0b3c78f0bfecff7a92bcdcd49193
mutant.observed: copy BEFORE = 5446cab64636e0dd8bcc79bc8e287a39 (mtime 2026-09-03 03:49:23.411749500 -0400); copy AFTER touch = abebfe86ed457936a83caa7381fc7ea2 (mtime 2026-09-03 04:16:58.614782500 -0400), size unchanged at 82,661,376 B -- FINGERPRINT CHANGED. Real canonical read by the same method at the same instant = 711b0b3c78f0bfecff7a92bcdcd49193, UNCHANGED. So the method discriminates, and the canonical's clean reading is a REAL NEGATIVE rather than a blind instrument.
